**Finding resubmitted: compliant — no redline, no comment (correct for a compliant finding).**

What changed in the repair:

- **Stated the inapplicability of the failing check explicitly.** The "audit frequency limited" deterministic test fails only because there is no audit clause to carry a frequency cap. I recorded that as an artifact of absence, and confirmed the walk-away triggers (unlimited/unannounced audits, remote access to Customer systems) are not met because no audit or access right is granted at all.
- **Documented the negative-search evidence.** No hits for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "monitor" or "premises"; "records" appears only in the § 9.1 liability carve-out. Ruled out each section that could plausibly host a verification right — §§ 4.1/4.2, 11.5, 12.1, 13.2 and §§ 14.1–14.20.
- **Pinned the § 11.3 analysis to the full paragraph range** (p0132–p0137, cited p0132/p0133/p0137): a breach-remedy provision tied to the § 11.2(b) content warranties, conferring no access to our systems, personnel, books or records and no audit cost or cooperation burden.
- **Kept the § 11.3 point as a residual observation,** with a forward-looking trigger: if § 11.3 is ever expanded to reach Customer records or systems, this rule should be re-run.

No redline was proposed, since inserting frequency, notice or cost limits would create an audit right in IBM's favour that the contract does not currently give it.
